passages.text: Then Jesus told them a parable about their need to pray at all times and not lose heart: “In a certain town there was a judge who neither feared God nor respected men.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He told them a parable.
He wanted them to know they must always pray.
He told them not to lose heart.
He said there was a judge in a certain town.
This judge did not fear God.
This judge did not respect people.
passages.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς πρὸς τὸ δεῖν πάντοτε προσεύχεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ μὴ ἐνκακεῖν λέγων Κριτής τις ἦν ἔν τινι πόλει τὸν Θεὸν μὴ φοβούμενος καὶ ἄνθρωπον μὴ ἐντρεπόμενος

passages.text: And there was a widow in that town who kept appealing to him, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’
passages.sermon: A widow lived in that town.\r\nShe went to the judge again and again.\r\nShe said to him, “Give me justice against my adversary.”
passages.original: χήρα δὲ ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἐκείνῃ καὶ ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτὸν λέγουσα Ἐκδίκησόν με ἀπὸ τοῦ ἀντιδίκου μου

passages.text: For a while he refused, but later he said to himself, ‘Though I neither fear God nor respect men, yet because this widow keeps pestering me, I will give her justice. Then she will stop wearing me out with her perpetual requests.’ ”
passages.sermon:
A judge lived in a certain town.
This judge did not fear God.
He did not respect people.
A widow in that town kept coming to him.
She asked him for justice against her adversary.
For a while, the judge refused to help her.
Later, the judge spoke to himself.
He said, “I do not fear God.
I do not respect people.
But this widow keeps bothering me.
She is causing me trouble.
I will give her justice.
Then she will stop coming to me all the time.
She will not wear me out with her constant requests.”
passages.original: Καὶ οὐκ ἤθελεν ἐπὶ χρόνον μετὰ ταῦτα δὲ εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ Εἰ καὶ τὸν Θεὸν οὐ φοβοῦμαι οὐδὲ ἄνθρωπον ἐντρέπομαι διά γε τὸ παρέχειν μοι κόπον τὴν χήραν ταύτην ἐκδικήσω αὐτήν ἵνα μὴ εἰς τέλος ἐρχομένη ὑπωπιάζῃ με

passages.text: And the Lord said, “Listen to the words of the unjust judge.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus is the Lord.
He said, "Listen to what the unjust judge says."
The judge does not act justly.
Pay attention to his words.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Κύριος Ἀκούσατε τί ὁ κριτὴς τῆς ἀδικίας λέγει

passages.text: Will not God bring about justice for His elect who cry out to Him day and night? Will He continue to defer their help?
passages.sermon:
God is just.
God has chosen people.
These chosen people cry out to God.
They call to Him day and night.
God hears them.
God is patient with them.
God will not ignore their cries.
God will bring them justice.
God will not delay to help them.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Θεὸς οὐ μὴ ποιήσῃ τὴν ἐκδίκησιν τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν αὐτοῦ τῶν βοώντων αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός καὶ μακροθυμεῖ ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς

passages.text: I tell you, He will promptly carry out justice on their behalf. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on earth?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus is the Son of God.
He said, “God will act quickly for His chosen people.
God will bring justice for them.
God’s chosen people cry out to Him day and night.
God will not delay to help them.
But when the Son of Man comes,
will He find faith on earth?”
passages.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ποιήσει τὴν ἐκδίκησιν αὐτῶν ἐν τάχει πλὴν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐλθὼν ἆρα εὑρήσει τὴν πίστιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς

passages.text: To some who trusted in their own righteousness and viewed others with contempt, He also told this parable: “Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to certain people.
These people trusted in their own righteousness.
They looked down on others.
Jesus told them a parable.
Two men went up to the temple to pray.
One man was a Pharisee.
The other man was a tax collector.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ καὶ πρός τινας τοὺς πεποιθότας ἐφ’ ἑαυτοῖς ὅτι εἰσὶν δίκαιοι καὶ ἐξουθενοῦντας τοὺς λοιποὺς τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην Ἄνθρωποι δύο ἀνέβησαν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν προσεύξασθαι ὁ εἷς Φαρισαῖος καὶ ὁ ἕτερος τελώνης

passages.text: The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed, ‘God, I thank You that I am not like the other men—swindlers, evildoers, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.
passages.sermon:
A Pharisee was a religious leader among the Jews.
He trusted in his own righteousness.
He looked down on others.
The Pharisee stood alone in the temple.
He prayed to God.
He said, “God, I thank You.”
He said, “I am not like other men.”
He said, “Other men are swindlers.”
He said, “Other men are evildoers.”
He said, “Other men are adulterers.”
He said, “I am not like this tax collector.”
passages.original: ὁ Φαρισαῖος σταθεὶς ταῦτα πρὸς ἑαυτὸν προσηύχετο Ὁ Θεός εὐχαριστῶ σοι ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ὥσπερ οἱ λοιποὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἅρπαγες ἄδικοι μοιχοί ἢ καὶ ὡς οὗτος ὁ τελώνης

passages.text: I fast twice a week and pay tithes of all that I acquire.’
passages.sermon: The Pharisee spoke about himself to God.\r\nHe said, “I fast twice every week.\r\nI give a tenth of everything I get.”
passages.original: νηστεύω δὶς τοῦ σαββάτου ἀποδεκατῶ πάντα ὅσα κτῶμαι

passages.text: But the tax collector stood at a distance, unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his breast and said, ‘God, have mercy on me, a sinner!’
passages.sermon:
The tax collector stood far away from others.
He did not want to lift his eyes up to heaven.
He beat his chest.
He said, “God, have mercy on me, a sinner.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ τελώνης μακρόθεν ἑστὼς οὐκ ἤθελεν οὐδὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ἐπᾶραι εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν ἀλλ’ ἔτυπτεν τὸ στῆθος αὐτοῦ λέγων Ὁ Θεός ἱλάσθητί μοι τῷ ἁμαρτωλῷ

passages.text: I tell you, this man, rather than the Pharisee, went home justified. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus compared the tax collector and the Pharisee.
Jesus said the tax collector went home justified.
The Pharisee did not go home justified.
God justifies the humble person.
Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled.
Everyone who humbles himself will be exalted.
passages.original: λέγω ὑμῖν κατέβη οὗτος δεδικαιωμένος εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ παρ’ ἐκεῖνον ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται ὁ δὲ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται

passages.text: Now people were even bringing their babies to Jesus for Him to place His hands on them. And when the disciples saw this, they rebuked those who brought them.
passages.sermon:
People brought their babies to Jesus.
They wanted Jesus to touch their babies.
The disciples saw this.
The disciples rebuked the people who brought the babies.
passages.original: Προσέφερον δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ τὰ βρέφη ἵνα αὐτῶν ἅπτηται ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐπετίμων αὐτοῖς

passages.text: But Jesus called the children to Him and said, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them! For the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw people bringing children to Him.
Jesus called the children to Himself.
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said, “Let the little children come to Me.”
He said, “Do not stop them.”
He said, “The kingdom of God belongs to people like these children.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσεκαλέσατο αὐτὰ λέγων Ἄφετε τὰ παιδία ἔρχεσθαι πρός με καὶ μὴ κωλύετε αὐτά τῶν γὰρ τοιούτων ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: Truly I tell you, anyone who does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said something very important.
He said, “I tell you the truth.”
A person must receive the kingdom of God like a little child.
If a person does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child, that person will never enter it.
The kingdom of God belongs to those who receive it with childlike trust and humility.
passages.original: ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὃς ἂν μὴ δέξηται τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ ὡς παιδίον οὐ μὴ εἰσέλθῃ εἰς αὐτήν

passages.text: Then a certain ruler asked Him, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
passages.sermon: A certain ruler spoke to Jesus.\r\nThe ruler asked Jesus a question.\r\nThe ruler said, “Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπηρώτησέν τις αὐτὸν ἄρχων λέγων Διδάσκαλε ἀγαθέ τί ποιήσας ζωὴν αἰώνιον κληρονομήσω

passages.text: “Why do you call Me good?” Jesus replied. “No one is good except God alone.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the ruler.
Jesus asked, “Why do you call Me good?”
Only God is good.
No one else is good except God.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ Θεός

passages.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not commit adultery, do not murder, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and mother.’”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the ruler.
Jesus said, “You know the commandments.”
Do not commit adultery.
Do not murder.
Do not steal.
Do not bear false witness.
Honor your father.
Honor your mother.
passages.original: τὰς ἐντολὰς οἶδας Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς Μὴ φονεύσῃς Μὴ κλέψῃς Μὴ ψευδομαρτυρήσῃς Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα

passages.text: “All these I have kept from my youth,” he said.
passages.sermon: A man spoke to Jesus.\r\nHe said he had obeyed all the commandments.\r\nHe said he had done this since he was young.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ταῦτα πάντα ἐφύλαξα ἐκ νεότητος μου

passages.text: On hearing this, Jesus told him, “You still lack one thing: Sell everything you own and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus had listened to the man say he kept all the commandments since youth.
Jesus said, “You still lack one thing.
Sell everything you own.
Give what you have to the poor.
You will have treasure in heaven.
Then come.
Follow Me.”
passages.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἔτι ἕν σοι λείπει πάντα ὅσα ἔχεις πώλησον καὶ διάδος πτωχοῖς καὶ ἕξεις θησαυρὸν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς καὶ δεῦρο ἀκολούθει μοι

passages.text: But when the ruler heard this, he became very sad, because he was extremely wealthy.
passages.sermon: The ruler heard what Jesus said.\r\nHe became very sad.\r\nHe was extremely wealthy.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας ταῦτα περίλυπος ἐγενήθη ἦν γὰρ πλούσιος σφόδρα

passages.text: Seeing the man’s sadness, Jesus said, “How hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of God!
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the man become very sad.
The man was extremely wealthy.
Jesus spoke to him.
Jesus said, "It is very hard for people who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God."
passages.original: Ἰδὼν δὲ αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς περίλυπον γενόμενον εἶπεν Πῶς δυσκόλως οἱ τὰ χρήματα ἔχοντες εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσπορεύονται

passages.text: Indeed, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus explained a truth about the rich.
A camel is a large animal.
A needle has a very small opening called the eye.
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle.
It is harder for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
passages.original: εὐκοπώτερον γάρ ἐστιν κάμηλον διὰ τρήματος βελόνης εἰσελθεῖν ἢ πλούσιον εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν

passages.text: Those who heard this asked, “Who then can be saved?”
passages.sermon:
Some people listened to Jesus.
They heard what Jesus said about the rich and the kingdom of God.
These people asked a question.
They said, “Who can be saved?”
passages.original: Εἶπαν δὲ οἱ ἀκούσαντες Καὶ τίς δύναται σωθῆναι

passages.text: But Jesus said, “What is impossible with man is possible with God.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said this truth.
Some things are impossible for people.
God can do what people cannot do.
What is impossible for people is possible for God.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Τὰ ἀδύνατα παρὰ ἀνθρώποις δυνατὰ παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ ἐστιν

passages.text: “Look,” said Peter, “we have left all we had to follow You.”
passages.sermon:
Peter spoke to Jesus.
Peter said, “Look at us.”
Peter and the other disciples left everything they owned.
Peter and the others chose to follow Jesus.
passages.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Πέτρος Ἰδοὺ ἡμεῖς ἀφέντες τὰ ἴδια ἠκολουθήσαμέν σοι

passages.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “no one who has left home or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God will fail to receive many times more in this age—and in the age to come, eternal life.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus said, “Truly, I tell you this.
No one leaves home for the sake of the kingdom of God.
No one leaves wife, brothers, parents, or children for the sake of the kingdom of God.
That person will receive many times more in this present age.
That person will also receive eternal life in the age to come.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδείς ἐστιν ὃς ἀφῆκεν οἰκίαν ἢ γυναῖκα ἢ ἀδελφοὺς ἢ γονεῖς ἢ τέκνα ἕνεκεν τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ ὃς οὐχὶ μὴ ἀπολάβῃ πολλαπλασίονα ἐν τῷ καιρῷ τούτῳ καὶ ἐν τῷ αἰῶνι τῷ ἐρχομένῳ ζωὴν αἰώνιον

passages.text: Then Jesus took the Twelve aside and said to them, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything the prophets have written about the Son of Man will be fulfilled.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was the teacher and leader of the disciples.
He took the Twelve disciples aside.
He spoke directly to them.
He said, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem.
Everything written by the prophets about the Son of Man will happen.
All these things will be fulfilled.”
passages.original: Παραλαβὼν δὲ τοὺς δώδεκα εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ καὶ τελεσθήσεται πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα διὰ τῶν προφητῶν τῷ Υἱῷ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: He will be delivered over to the Gentiles and will be mocked and insulted and spit upon.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about Himself, the Son of Man.
He said the Son of Man will be handed over to the Gentiles.
The Gentiles will mock Him.
They will insult Him.
They will spit on Him.
passages.original: παραδοθήσεται γὰρ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν καὶ ἐμπαιχθήσεται καὶ ὑβρισθήσεται καὶ ἐμπτυσθήσεται

passages.text: They will flog Him and kill Him, and on the third day He will rise again.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about Himself, the Son of Man.
People will flog Him.
They will kill Him.
On the third day, He will rise again.
passages.original: καὶ μαστιγώσαντες ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν καὶ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῇ τρίτῃ ἀναστήσεται

passages.text: But the disciples did not understand any of these things. The meaning was hidden from them, and they did not comprehend what He was saying.
passages.sermon:
The disciples followed Jesus.
Jesus told them what would happen to Him.
The disciples did not understand any of these things.
The meaning of His words was hidden from them.
They did not comprehend what Jesus was saying.
passages.original: Καὶ αὐτοὶ οὐδὲν τούτων συνῆκαν καὶ ἦν τὸ ῥῆμα τοῦτο κεκρυμμένον ἀπ’ αὐτῶν καὶ οὐκ ἐγίνωσκον τὰ λεγόμενα

passages.text: As Jesus drew near to Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
passages.sermon: Jesus was approaching Jericho.\r\nA blind man sat beside the road.\r\nThe blind man was begging.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ ἐγγίζειν αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰεριχὼ τυφλός τις ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ἐπαιτῶν

passages.text: When he heard the crowd going by, he asked what was happening.
passages.sermon: A blind man sat beside the road near Jericho.\r\nHe heard a crowd passing by.\r\nHe asked what was happening.
passages.original: ἀκούσας δὲ ὄχλου διαπορευομένου ἐπυνθάνετο τί εἴη τοῦτο

passages.text: “Jesus of Nazareth is passing by,” they told him.
passages.sermon:
A blind man sat beside the road near Jericho.
He was begging.
A crowd passed by him.
He asked what was happening.
People answered him.
They said, “Jesus of Nazareth is passing by.”
passages.original: Ἀπήγγειλαν δὲ αὐτῷ ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος παρέρχεται

passages.text: So he called out, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
passages.sermon:
A blind man sat by the roadside.
He heard a crowd passing by.
He learned that Jesus of Nazareth was coming.
He called out loudly.
He said, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐβόησεν λέγων Ἰησοῦ υἱὲ Δαυίδ ἐλέησόν με

passages.text: Those who led the way admonished him to be silent, but he cried out all the louder, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
passages.sermon:
Some people walked in front of Jesus.
These people led the way.
They told the blind man to be quiet.
They warned him not to speak.
The blind man did not stay silent.
He shouted even louder.
He said, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
passages.original: Καὶ οἱ προάγοντες ἐπετίμων αὐτῷ ἵνα σιγήσῃ αὐτὸς δὲ πολλῷ μᾶλλον ἔκραζεν Υἱὲ Δαυίδ ἐλέησόν με

passages.text: Jesus stopped and directed that the man be brought to Him. When he had been brought near, Jesus asked him, “What do you want Me to do for you?” “Lord,” he said, “let me see again.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was traveling.
A blind man called out to Jesus for mercy.
Jesus stopped.
Jesus told others to bring the blind man to Him.
They brought the blind man to Jesus.
Jesus spoke to the blind man.
Jesus asked, “What do you want Me to do for you?”
The blind man answered Jesus.
He said, “Lord, let me see again.”
passages.original: Σταθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκέλευσεν αὐτὸν ἀχθῆναι πρὸς αὐτόν ἐγγίσαντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν Τί σοι θέλεις ποιήσω Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Κύριε ἵνα ἀναβλέψω

passages.text: “Receive your sight!” Jesus replied. “Your faith has healed you.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the man who was blind.\r\nJesus said, “Receive your sight.”\r\nJesus said, “Your faith has healed you.”
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἀνάβλεψον ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε

passages.text: Immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus, glorifying God. And all the people who saw this gave praise to God.
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed the blind man immediately.
The man could see at once.
He followed Jesus.
He gave glory to God.
All the people saw what happened.
They praised God.
passages.original: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀνέβλεψεν καὶ ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ δοξάζων τὸν Θεόν καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἰδὼν ἔδωκεν αἶνον τῷ Θεῷ
